stories.title: ICE plans to equip agents with gloves that can deliver electric shocks
stories.summary: The US immigration agency is spending $20m on gloves that deliver a sharp electric shock intended to compel subjects to comply.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: ICE plans to equip agents with gloves that can deliver electric shocks. The US immigration agency is spending $20m on gloves that deliver a sharp electric shock intended to compel subjects to comply. Source: BBC World.
article_sentences: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers may soon be equipped with gloves that can deliver electric shocks as they carry out their law enforcement duties.
ICE plans to spend up to $20m (£14.8m) to buy the Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter (GLOVE), according to a note published on Monday by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
The gloves can deliver up to 380 volts of electricity, roughly three times the charge of a standard US power outlet.
Civil rights groups, including the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), have expressed alarm over its use.

"ICE is constantly assessing the needs of our officers in the field to ensure they have the tools and equipment necessary to safely arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our country," the DHS said in a statement to the BBC.
Compliant Technologies LLC, which makes the gloves, told the BBC it was unable to comment on the sale.
A no-bid purchase contract could be published as early as Friday, DHS said.
The GLOVE devices are activated by pushing a button to deliver shocks and can deliver up to 30 pulses per second.
They also feature built-in microprocessors that keep a record of activation.
Compliant Technologies states on its website that they do not cause injury and are used by many agencies.

A user manual on the company's website recommends avoiding use on the elderly, small children, pregnant women and the "severely handicapped", as well as that an additional officer be present to restrain the subject while the gloves are being used.
Unlike a taser, which uses sharp barbs in the skin to deliver a shock of up to 50,000 volts, the gloves do not complete an electrical circuit inside the body.
